notes:
Summary: RadialThrust is a programmatic adtech vendor that needs sub-100ms end-to-end inference for personalization and reranking in production. High QPS spikes during bid windows; cost is critical. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Optimize for batching/caching/quantization.

Requirements / goals (from CTO call):
- P95 latency target: <= 50ms for 256-token context on production mix (short prompts + user profile prefixes).
- Sustained throughput target: 600 reqs/sec with 2x burst capacity during peak auctions.
- Unit cost target: reduce inference cost by ~30% vs current in-house A10G cluster.
- Deterministic tail behavior: must stay under SLA during cache misses. Quote from CTO: "If p95 isn't deterministic under 60ms during peak we can't switch vendors."

Technical preferences and asks:
- Model candidates: 7B/13B open models, quantized variants (INT8 / 4-bit weight-only) as primary fallbacks. Prefer ability to route to smaller quantized variant automatically on overload.
- Caching: aggressive prefix & KV cache reuse for repeated user sessions; ability to pin warm cache for high-value users. Need hooks to measure cold vs warm latencies.
- Batching: dynamic batching with target batch sizes 16-64 depending on latency window; want Redwood Optimize suggestions for optimal batch policy by hour-of-day.
- Quantization: interest in Redwood recommendations for mixed-precision (INT8 runtime; weight-only INT4 for 7B) and expected perf/cost delta.
- Benchmarking: want Redwood perf harness (wrk-style) and a reproducible benchmark plan to compare Dedicated(A10G) vs our in-house and Redwood-hosted. Need metrics: p50/p95/p99, cold-start tail, tokens/sec, GPU-util, cost-per-token.
- Observability: per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and SLO alerting tied to perf tests.

Operational notes / risk:
- Security team requires SSO/SAML, KMS integration and a short security questionnaire answered (Drive doc linked).
- NDA for sample logs needed before we run full POC dataset.
- Blocker: unclear fallback routing semantics for partial model degradations; SE to confirm behavior.

Internal next steps (AE notes):
- Diego to run initial perf plan with Redwood perf team week of 2025-02-10.
- Put together sample workload files (auction traces) — RTPL to supply by 2025-02-07 under NDA.
- SE to confirm quantization recommendations and expected cost delta by 2025-02-12.

Customer quote on call 2025-01-22: "We need predictable tail latency more than absolute lowest median. Cost improvements are nice if we can keep the auction window deterministic."
